Total number of questions — 20
171
Effect of earthquake
*541. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of EARTH SCIENCES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Northern
India was rocked by earthquake recently;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have identified
earthquake prone areas in the country;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether the local administration of
these areas has been advised about the type
of construction to be carried out in these
areas to withstand the effect of earthquakes;
and
(f) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Private participation in power sector
*542. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that despite
repeated attempts by Government to
enthuse the private sector, it accounts for
just 11 per cent of the country's total power
generation capacity of 1,28,182 mw;
(b) whether it is a fact that as the sale of
electricity is not governed by the laws of
the market, and the distribution sector is
still reeling under losses, the private players
are reluctant to invest money; and
(c) if so, the steps Government propose
to take to promote the private participation
in power sector?
Reconstitution of State Electricity
Boards
†*543. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) the number of States where
Electricity Boards have been constituted
separately for generation, transmission and
distribution of electricity under the
Electricity Act, 2003;
(b) which States have not constituted
separate Boards;
(c) the reasons stated by the States for
non-constitution of the Boards; and
(d) the action taken against the States
which have not constituted these Boards?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

172
Power situation in Rajasthan
*544. DR. GY AN PRAKASH
PILANIA: Will the Minister of POWER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether power shortage is
hampering industrial and agricultural growth
in Rajasthan;
(b) if so, the total demand and supply
of power in rural/urban/tribal/hilly/desert
areas of Rajasthan, during the last three
years, year-wise and sector-wise
(industrial, agricultural, commercial and
domestic etc.);
(c) the power scenario, at present in
Rajasthan;
(d) the measures initiated/contemplated
to meet power shortage;
(e) the financial allocations made for the
purpose  by the Centre;
(f) whether any proposals from
Rajasthan regarding power generation are
pending with the Centre; and
(g) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken thereon?
Setting up of High Court Bench at
Dharamsala
*545. SHRI SURESH BHARDWAJ:
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have received
any proposal from State Government of
Himachal Pradesh to establish a Bench of
High Court of Himachal Pradesh at
Dharamsala;
(b) if so, the action taken thereon; and
(c) if not, whether Government will
favourably pursue the proposal as and when
the same is received?
Cases pending in Supreme Court
*546. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will
the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of cases pending in the
Supreme Court as on 31st March, 2007;
(b) what is their State-wise break-up;
(c) what is the year-wise pendency for
the last ten years; and
(d) whether any special steps are
proposed to be taken to liquidate this
pendency like late sittings introduced in
Vadodara and Ahmedabad districts of
Gujarat since November, 2006?
NTPC's power project in Sri Lanka
*547. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the
Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Power Finance Corporation
Limited has proposed to finance NTPC's
Power Project in Sri Lanka;
(b) if so, what is the project cost and
the stage of the project; and
(c) whether the recent encounter
between LTTE and Sri Lankan army
followed by indiscriminate attack on
innocent Shri Lankan Tamils by Sri Lankan
army will affect the trade and commerce
intercourse between these two countries?
Separate syllabus in Kendriya

the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE

(a) whether there are separate syllabus
in Kendriya Vidyalayas and the schools of
the State Governments;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and
whether it is not a discriminatory policy to

————
List of Questions for  WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday,  the May 14, 2007/Vaisakha 24, 1929 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Earth Sciences; Food Processing Industries; Human Resource
Development; Law and Justice; Mines; Minority Affairs; New and Renewable
Energy; Power; Science and Technology; Social Justice and Empowerment;
Tribal Affairs; Women and Child Development)
Total number of questions — 155
957
Impact of climate change
4122. SHRI RAHUL BAJAJ:
SHRI RAJKUMAR
DHOOT:
Will the Minister of EARTH
SCIENCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the UN's
IPCC on April 6, 2007 has categorically
mentioned India as a high risk area about
the impact of climate change in India; and
(b) if so, the steps being taken to, at
least, monitor parameters relating to the
melting of glaciers in the Himalayan ranges?
Report on climate change
forecasting
4123. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the
Minister of EARTH SCIENCES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the most shocking U.N. Panel report on
the climate change forecasting that India
would be among countries, worst affected
by global warming;
(b) the ill-effects and dangers forecasted
against India; and
(c) whether the U.N. Panel Report on
this aspect is reliable and scientific?
U.N. Panel Report on global warming
4124. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the
Minister of EARTH SCIENCES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the U.N. Panel Report on
global warming has been considered
seriously or ignored by other countries;
(b) the reaction of India on this report;
and
(c) whether there will be any preventive
or curative process and the measures to get
over this nature's onslaught?
Wastage of fruits and vegetables in
the country
4125. SHRI S. ANBALAGAN: Will the
Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
about 60 thousand tonnes of fruits and
vegetables are going to waste due to lack of
processing facilities in the country;

958
(b) if so, the details thereof and the steps
proposed to be taken by Government
alongwith the State Governments to
process fruits and vegetables that go waste
and use them for the poor people;
(c) whether Government propose to
create opportunity for unemployed youths
in the processing of fruits and vegetables
that go waste; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Setting up of Food Safety and
Standard Authority
of India
4126. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
SHRIMATI SUPRIYA
SULE:
Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether his Ministry has decided to
set up the Food Safety and Standard
Authority of India which has been a long
standing demand of the industry, to
facilitate the implementation of the Food
Safety and Standards Act, 2006;
(b) whether Food Safety and Standards
Bill, 2005 became an Act on 23rd August,
2006 but it cannot be implemented without
the setting up of FSSAI;
(c) if so, by when a final decision in
setting up Food Safety and Standard
Authority of India is likely to be taken;
and
(d) the extent to which it will be
helpful?
Food processing for agri-products
4127. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) the total per cent of agri-products,
which are being processed in the Food
Processing Industries in different States and
the details thereof, State-wise and item-
wise; and
(b) the steps being taken to increase
further food processing of different agri
products?
Adoption of Vision Document 2015 for
food processing sector
4128. SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI: Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether 'Vision 2015', adopted by
Government for the food processing sector,
envisages India's potential to achieve 3 per
cent share in world trade of agricultural and
food products;
(b) if so, the efforts been made by
Government to enhance productivity in
different States particularly in Uttar
Pradesh and Chhattisgarh;
(c) the share of Uttar Pradesh and
Chhattisgarh separately in total
productivity;
(d) how much money has been invested
in these States on R&D relating to food
pocessing technology and what is the result
thereof; and
(e) the incentives provided to mango
growers in the States so far?

959
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Survey on quantity of fruits
4129. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will
the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
conducted any survey to establish the total
quantity of fruits available for food
processing industries in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether a huge quantity of fruits is
wasted every year due to non-existence of
proper storage facility of the country; and
(d) if so, the details thereof, and the
steps being taken in this regard?
Chemicals and compounds in soft
drinks

CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of
FOOD PROCES
